text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Austria's new Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima wants to raise employment, guarantee social security and provide a "modern" Austria. Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel spoke of a "constructive new beginning" of the government.
- New Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch wants to find compensation for the abolished minimum corporate tax to ensure the government's austerity measures are socially equal.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner says plans by Austria's energy industry to reorganise the market ahead of its liberalisation will not solve structural problems.
- Skimaker Kaestle, owned by Italy's Benetton group, is to halve the number of its employees and to stop production by April.
DIE PRESSE
- Schuessel wants the government to work together like one company, saying the new Social Democrat government team is the last chance for the coalition.
- Raiffeisen Oberoesterreich bank chief Ludwig Scharinger expects a joint bid of Raiffeisen and investor Hannes Androsch's group for Austrian salt producer Salinen AG to win.
- Karl Wlaschek, former boss of retail chain Billa plans to take over Creditanstalt's real estate unit.
- The fusion of Swiss chemical giants Ciba and Sandoz is bringing benefits to Austria as the merged company Novartis plans to upgrade its Austrian research centre.
- Austria is Hungary's second most important trade partner, having invested over 22 billion schillings in the country so far.
KURIER
- New chancellor Klima was sworn in yesterday. The government is now looking into the functions of different ministries to make their work more efficient.
- Flughafen Wien's dividend is to remain at the same level for 1996 as in 1995, eventhough earnings were lower.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Turnover in Austria's tourism industry was up 7.5 percent in November and December 1996.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Windowmaker Internorm is planning to build a new production plant worth 700 million schillings by the year 2000.
- Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberoesterreich chief Ludwig Scharinger is against closer ties between Raiffeisen and Volksbanken.
